    latex_engine: xelatex

```{r analysis, message=FALSE}
library(atrrr)
# COLLECTING OUR POSTS ====

start_date <- "2025-09-28"
end_date <- "2026-09-30"


#Searching for relevant post material on bluesky
ai_posts <- search_skeet(
  "AI",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

dim(ai_posts)
names(ai_posts)


artificial_intelligence_posts <- search_skeet(
  "artificial intelligence",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

chatgpt_posts <- search_skeet(
  "ChatGPT",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

openai_posts <- search_skeet(
  "OpenAI",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

generative_ai_posts <- search_skeet(
  "generative AI",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

llm_posts <- search_skeet(
  "LLM",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

machine_learning_posts <- search_skeet(
  "machine learning",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)

large_language_model_posts <- search_skeet(
  "large language model",
  sort = "latest",
  since = start_date,
  until = end_date,
  limit = 200
)



# Combining the posts into one database

# Combine all search results into one master dataset.
ai_posts_all <- rbind(
  ai_posts,
  artificial_intelligence_posts,
  chatgpt_posts,
  openai_posts,
  generative_ai_posts,
  machine_learning_posts,
  large_language_model_posts,
  llm_posts
)


#Removing duplicate posts

ai_posts_all <- ai_posts_all[!duplicated(ai_posts_all$uri), ]

dim(ai_posts_all)

str(ai_posts_all[, c("author_handle", "mentions", "in_reply_to", "quotes")])

# Checking for missing values in variables

sum(is.na(ai_posts_all$text))

sum(is.na(ai_posts_all$like_count))

sum(is.na(ai_posts_all$reply_count))

sum(is.na(ai_posts_all$repost_count))

sum(is.na(ai_posts_all$indexed_at))
sum(is.null(ai_posts_all$tags))

sum(ai_posts_all$text == "")
sum(!is.na(ai_posts_all$in_reply_to))
sum(!is.na(ai_posts_all$quotes))
sum(!sapply(ai_posts_all$mentions, is.null))

ai_text <- ai_posts_all$text
ai_text <- ai_text[ai_text != ""]
length(ai_text)
# Count posts with empty text.
sum(ai_posts_all$text == "")

# Display the first 20 text values.
head(ai_posts_all$text, 20)

# Count zero-like posts.
sum(ai_posts_all$like_count == 0)

# Count zero-reply posts.
sum(ai_posts_all$reply_count == 0)

# Count zero-repost posts.
sum(ai_posts_all$repost_count == 0)



# Create a dataset containing only posts with text.
ai_text_data <- ai_posts_all[ai_posts_all$text != "", ]

# Check how many posts remain.
nrow(ai_text_data)



#Cleaning the data

ai_clean <- ai_posts_all

# Count how many duplicate post URIs exist.
sum(duplicated(ai_clean$uri))
dim(ai_clean)
sum(duplicated(ai_clean$uri))


# Create a dataset containing only posts with actual text.
ai_text <- ai_clean[ai_clean$text != "", ]

# Check how many posts remain.
nrow(ai_text)


# Count posts that contain only whitespace.
sum(trimws(ai_clean$text) == "")
# Keep posts that contain actual text after removing surrounding whitespace.
ai_text <- ai_clean[trimws(ai_clean$text) != "", ]

# Check the number of usable text posts.
nrow(ai_text)
sum(trimws(ai_clean$text) == "")



#text preprocessing

library(tm)
library(SnowballC)

# Creating a corpus from the text of our Bluesky posts.
ai_corpus <- Corpus(
  VectorSource(ai_text$text)
)

ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  content_transformer(tolower)
)
length(ai_corpus)

# Remove URLs from the posts.
ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  content_transformer(function(x) gsub("http[^[:space:]]*", "", x))
)

ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  removeNumbers
)

ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  removePunctuation
)
#Removing filler words (stopwords)
custom_stopwords <- c(
  stopwords("en"),
  "use",
  "like",
  "can",
  "just",
  "new",
  "will",
  "make",
  "get",
  "also",
  "much",
  "one",
  "still"
)

ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  removeWords,
  custom_stopwords
)

ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  stripWhitespace
)

ai_corpus <- tm_map(
  ai_corpus,
  stemDocument,
  language = "english"
)


inspect(ai_corpus[1])
inspect(ai_corpus[1:5])

# Display the number of documents in the cleaned corpus.
length(ai_corpus)


# Create a Term-Document Matrix from our cleaned corpus.
ai_tdm <- TermDocumentMatrix(ai_corpus)

dim(ai_tdm)


# Convert the TDM into a standard R matrix.
ai_matrix <- as.matrix(ai_tdm)

dim(ai_matrix)
word_frequency <- rowSums(ai_matrix)
head(word_frequency, 20)

word_frequency_sorted <- sort(
  word_frequency,
  decreasing = TRUE
)
head(word_frequency_sorted, 20)






library(wordcloud)

top80_words <- head(word_frequency_sorted, 80)

# Display the top 80 words and their frequencies.
top80_words
wordcloud(
  words = names(top80_words),
  freq = as.numeric(top80_words),
  min.freq = 1,
  max.words = 80,
  random.order = FALSE
)
# TFIDF weighted wordcloud

ai_tfidf <- weightTfIdf(ai_tdm)

# Convert the TF-IDF weighted matrix into a standard R matrix.
ai_tfidf_matrix <- as.matrix(ai_tfidf)

# Calculate the total TF-IDF weight for each term.
tfidf_frequency <- rowSums(ai_tfidf_matrix)


# Sort the terms from highest to lowest TF-IDF weight.
tfidf_frequency_sorted <- sort(
  tfidf_frequency,
  decreasing = TRUE
)

# Display the 20 terms with the highest overall TF-IDF weight.
head(tfidf_frequency_sorted, 20)


# Select the 80 terms with the highest TF-IDF weights.
top80_tfidf <- head(tfidf_frequency_sorted, 80)

# Create a word cloud using TF-IDF weights.
wordcloud(
  words = names(top80_tfidf),
  freq = as.numeric(top80_tfidf),
  min.freq = 1,
  max.words = 80,
  random.order = FALSE
)

# Making a bar chart for weighted results
library(ggplot2)

top20_frequency <- head(word_frequency_sorted, 20)

top20_frequency_df <- data.frame(
  term = names(top20_frequency),
  frequency = as.numeric(top20_frequency)
)

top20_frequency_df$term <- c(
    "OpenAI",
    "learning",
    "generative",
    "intelligence",
    "LLM",
    "machine",
    "ChatGPT",
    "model",
    "agent",
    "artificial",
    "Trump",
    "language",
    "large",
    "work",
    "now",
    "data",
    "say",
    "arXiv",
    "super",
    "people"
  )

ggplot(
  top20_frequency_df,
  aes(x = reorder(term, frequency), y = frequency)
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Most Frequently Discussed AI-Related Terms",
    x = "Term",
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

#Most frequently discussed AI-related terms are now visually represented on bar chart. OpenAI, learning and generative lead the terms. 




# RQ2

# Transpose TF-IDF so each row is one post.
ai_cluster_data <- t(ai_tfidf_matrix)

# Each TF-IDF row must correspond to the same row in ai_text.
stopifnot(nrow(ai_cluster_data) == nrow(ai_text))

# Remove empty TF-IDF rows from both datasets using the same index.
nonempty <- rowSums(abs(ai_cluster_data)) > 0
ai_cluster_data <- ai_cluster_data[nonempty, , drop = FALSE]
clustered_text_data <- ai_text[nonempty, , drop = FALSE]

# Normalize each post vector and calculate cosine distance.
post_norms <- sqrt(rowSums(ai_cluster_data^2))
stopifnot(all(post_norms > 0))
norm_ai_cluster_data <- sweep(ai_cluster_data, 1, post_norms, "/")
ai_cosine_distance <- dist(norm_ai_cluster_data, method = "euclidean")^2 / 2

# Create a two-dimensional representation of posts.
mds_ai <- cmdscale(ai_cosine_distance, k = 2)
stopifnot(nrow(mds_ai) == nrow(ai_cluster_data))

# Compare four and five clusters, then use k = 5 for RQ3 and RQ4.
set.seed(3020)
K4 <- kmeans(mds_ai, centers = 4, nstart = 10)
table(K4$cluster)

K5 <- kmeans(mds_ai, centers = 5, nstart = 10)
table(K5$cluster)

# Attach the five-cluster labels to their matching posts.
stopifnot(nrow(clustered_text_data) == length(K5$cluster))
clustered_text_data$cluster <- K5$cluster

# Inspect the highest-weight terms in each cluster.
for (cluster_id in 1:5) {
  clusterposts <- ai_cluster_data[K5$cluster == cluster_id, , drop = FALSE]
  clusterTermWeight <- colMeans(clusterposts)
  cat("\nCluster", cluster_id, "top terms:\n")
  print(head(sort(clusterTermWeight, decreasing = TRUE), 10))
}

# Plot the five clusters.
plot(
  mds_ai[, 1],
  mds_ai[, 2],
  col = K5$cluster,
  pch = 19,
  main = "AI Discussion Clusters",
  xlab = "MDS Dimension 1",
  ylab = "MDS Dimension 2"
)

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = paste("Cluster", 1:5),
  col = 1:5,
  pch = 19
)
#RQ3

dim(clustered_text_data)
names(clustered_text_data)

aggregate(
  like_count ~ cluster,
  data = clustered_text_data,
  FUN = mean
)

anova_model <- aov(
  like_count ~ factor(cluster),
  data = clustered_text_data
)

summary(anova_model)

boxplot(
  like_count ~ factor(cluster),
  data = clustered_text_data,
  xlab = "AI Discussion Cluster",
  ylab = "Number of Likes",
  main = "Like Engagement Across AI Discussion Clusters"
)



#RQ4
c(
  "Replies" = sum(!is.na(clustered_text_data$in_reply_to)),
  "Quotes" = sum(!is.na(clustered_text_data$quotes)),
  "Mentions" = sum(!sapply(clustered_text_data$mentions, is.null))
)
str(clustered_text_data[, c("in_reply_to", "quotes", "mentions")])
head(
  clustered_text_data[
    !is.na(clustered_text_data$in_reply_to) |
      !is.na(clustered_text_data$quotes),
    c("author_handle", "in_reply_to", "quotes")
  ],
  10
)
str(clustered_text_data$post_data[1])
clustered_text_data$mentions[
  which(!sapply(clustered_text_data$mentions, is.null))[1]
]
str(clustered_text_data$author_data[1])

author_map <- data.frame(
  did = sapply(clustered_text_data$author_data, function(x) x$did),
  handle = sapply(clustered_text_data$author_data, function(x) x$handle)
)

head(author_map)
sum(author_map$did %in% unlist(clustered_text_data$mentions))

sum(clustered_text_data$in_reply_to %in% clustered_text_data$uri, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(clustered_text_data$quotes %in% clustered_text_data$uri, na.rm = TRUE)

reply_target <- match(
  clustered_text_data$in_reply_to,
  clustered_text_data$uri
)

quote_target <- match(
  clustered_text_data$quotes,
  clustered_text_data$uri
)

sum(!is.na(reply_target))
sum(!is.na(quote_target))

reply_edges <- data.frame(
  from = clustered_text_data$author_handle[!is.na(reply_target)],
  to = clustered_text_data$author_handle[reply_target[!is.na(reply_target)]],
  type = "reply"
)

quote_edges <- data.frame(
  from = clustered_text_data$author_handle[!is.na(quote_target)],
  to = clustered_text_data$author_handle[quote_target[!is.na(quote_target)]],
  type = "quote"
)

interaction_edges <- rbind(
  reply_edges,
  quote_edges
)

nrow(interaction_edges)
head(interaction_edges)

interaction_edges <- interaction_edges[
  interaction_edges$from != interaction_edges$to,
]

nrow(interaction_edges)

library(igraph)

g <- graph_from_data_frame(
  interaction_edges,
  directed = TRUE
)

vcount(g)
ecount(g)

centrality <- data.frame(
  user = V(g)$name,
  in_degree = degree(g, mode = "in"),
  out_degree = degree(g, mode = "out"),
  betweenness = betweenness(g, directed = TRUE)
)

centrality <- centrality[
  order(-centrality$in_degree),
]

head(centrality, 10)

centrality_out <- centrality[
  order(-centrality$out_degree),
]

head(centrality_out, 10)

components(g, mode = "weak")

max(components(g, mode = "weak")$csize)
max(components(g, mode = "weak")$csize) / vcount(g) * 100


id_labels <- ifelse(
  degree(g, mode = "in") >= 2,
  V(g)$name,
  NA
)

plot(
  g,
  vertex.size = 5 + degree(g, mode = "in") * 2,
  vertex.label = id_labels,
  vertex.label.cex = 0.65,
  vertex.label.color = "black",
  vertex.label.dist = 1.2,
  edge.arrow.size = 0.25,
  main = "AI Discussion Interaction Network"
)
```
